subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which hormone lowers blood glucose concentration when it rises too high?
questions.explain: Insulin, released by the pancreas, causes cells to take up glucose and the liver to store it as glycogen, lowering blood glucose.

questions.q: How does the contraceptive pill (containing oestrogen/progesterone) prevent pregnancy?
options: It inhibits FSH so no eggs mature
It kills sperm directly in the uterus
questions.explain: The hormones in the pill inhibit FSH production, so no eggs mature and ovulation does not occur.

questions.q: Gametes (sex cells) such as sperm and egg are described as haploid because they contain:
options: Half the normal number of chromosomes (23 in humans)
Twice the normal number of chromosomes
questions.explain: Gametes are haploid, carrying a single set of chromosomes (23 in humans) so the full number is restored at fertilisation.

questions.q: A plant shoot grows towards light. This response is called:
questions.explain: Growth towards light is positive phototropism, controlled by the hormone auxin.

questions.q: Compared with nervous responses, hormonal responses are generally:
questions.explain: Hormonal responses are slower to act but their effects last longer than fast, short-lived nervous responses.

questions.q: Which hormone causes the lining of the uterus to thicken during the menstrual cycle?
questions.explain: Oestrogen, produced by the ovaries, causes the uterus lining to build up ready for a possible pregnancy.

questions.q: Which hormone controls how much water is reabsorbed in the kidney tubules?
questions.explain: ADH increases the permeability of kidney tubules so more water is reabsorbed when the body is dehydrated.

questions.q: A couple are using IVF. FSH and LH may be given to the woman first in order to:
options: Stimulate the maturation and release of several eggs
questions.explain: In IVF, FSH and LH stimulate the ovaries to mature several eggs, which are then collected and fertilised.

questions.q: How do plant roots respond to gravity?
options: They do not respond to gravity
questions.explain: Roots show positive gravitropism, growing downwards in the direction of gravity, controlled by auxin distribution.

questions.q: How does auxin cause a shoot to bend towards light?
options: Auxin builds up on the lit side, making it grow faster
Auxin destroys cells on the shaded side
Auxin builds up on the shaded side, making those cells elongate more
Auxin stops all growth on the lit side
questions.explain: Auxin accumulates on the shaded side and increases cell elongation there, bending the shoot towards the light.

questions.q: Type 2 diabetes is associated with:
options: Too much insulin being produced from birth
The body's cells no longer responding properly to insulin
A complete lack of a pancreas
questions.explain: In Type 2 diabetes cells stop responding to insulin; it is linked to obesity and often controlled by diet and exercise.

questions.q: On a hot day, a person sweats a lot and becomes dehydrated. How does the body respond to conserve water?
options: More ADH is released, so the kidneys reabsorb more water
questions.explain: When dehydrated, more ADH is released, making kidney tubules reabsorb more water, producing less, more concentrated urine.

questions.q: Hormones are transported around the body in the:
questions.explain: Hormones are chemical messengers secreted by glands and carried in the blood to target organs.

questions.q: What determines whether a human baby is biologically male or female?
options: Whether the sperm carries an X or Y chromosome
Whether the egg carries an X or Y chromosome
questions.explain: Eggs always carry X; the sperm carries either X (giving XX, female) or Y (giving XY, male), so the sperm determines sex.

questions.q: Sickle cell disease is an inherited disorder caused by a recessive allele. A person who is a carrier:
options: Always shows symptoms of the disease
Has one allele for it but does not show the disease, and can pass it on
Has the disease but cannot pass it on
questions.explain: A carrier is heterozygous: they carry one recessive allele without showing the disorder but can pass it to offspring.

questions.q: Which of these shows genetic variation rather than environmental variation?
options: A plant grown in shade being taller and thinner
A footballer's strong leg muscles from training
A person being tanned after sunbathing
questions.explain: Blood group is determined entirely by genes (genetic variation); the others are influenced by the environment.

questions.q: Cystic fibrosis is caused by a recessive allele. Two carrier parents (Ff × Ff) are crossed. What is the chance of a child having the disorder?
questions.explain: Two carriers (Ff × Ff) have a 1 in 4 chance of producing an affected ff child.

questions.q: During filtration in the kidney, which substance is NOT normally found in the filtrate of a healthy person?
questions.explain: Large proteins and blood cells are too big to be filtered, so they stay in the blood; glucose is filtered but reabsorbed.

questions.q: What is the genome of an organism?
options: The entire genetic material of that organism
questions.explain: The genome is the entire genetic material (all the DNA) of an organism.

questions.q: Which is a barrier method of contraception that also helps prevent STIs?
questions.explain: Condoms are a barrier method that physically stop sperm reaching the egg and also reduce STI transmission.

questions.q: Which organ monitors and controls blood glucose concentration by releasing insulin and glucagon?
questions.explain: The pancreas detects blood glucose levels and secretes insulin or glucagon to keep them within normal limits.

questions.q: What is the difference between genotype and phenotype?
options: They mean exactly the same thing
Genotype is the alleles present; phenotype is the physical characteristics
Genotype is the physical appearance; phenotype is the alleles
questions.explain: Genotype is the combination of alleles, while phenotype is the observable characteristic produced.
